text:
The treatment changes the outcome.
Results: Random assignment yielded a difference of 0.4, CI [0.2, 0.6].
premise: Random assignment yielded a difference of 0.4, CI [0.2, 0.6].
step: Random assignment and the estimated contrast support an effect on this measured outcome.
result: Support follows the claim; order is not a defect.

text:
Assignment was randomized.
Every participant improved.
Results: 40 of 100 participants improved.
step: Randomization does not establish universal improvement.
result: The universal claim does not follow from randomization and is contradicted by the reported count.

text:
Introduction: Assignment may affect measured trust.
Methods: Assignment was randomized.
Discussion: Assignment changed measured trust.
Results: The trust contrast was 0.4, CI [0.2, 0.6].
step: Use random assignment from Methods with the measured contrast from Results.
result: Support is distributed across sections; no missing-link criticism.

text: We extend Study A to older adults; Study A sampled younger adults (A).
claim: We extend Study A to older adults; Study A sampled younger adults (A).
step: The population difference establishes the stated extension, not superiority.
result: A single citation accurately supports this bounded relation.

text: Neither Study A nor Study B randomized assignment (A; B).
claim: Neither Study A nor Study B randomized assignment (A; B).
step: Citation multiplicity does not establish the design comparison.
result: The fetched Study B design refutes the comparison.

text: The mean measured outcome differed by 0.4, CI [0.2, 0.6].
claim: The mean measured outcome differed by 0.4, CI [0.2, 0.6].
step: The aggregate estimate suffices for the stated mean difference.
result: No individual example is required for this inference.

text:
The coded responses distinguish irony from literal agreement.
Only aggregate category counts are provided.
claim: The coded responses distinguish irony from literal agreement.
premise: Only aggregate category counts are provided.
step: Category counts alone cannot establish the coding distinction.
result: The bounded gap prevents assessing this coding inference, without establishing that authors failed to inspect cases.

text:
The coded responses distinguish irony from literal agreement.
The coding application is in the supplement.
supplement: Coding application: 'Great, another delay' is irony under the stated contextual rule.
claim: The coded responses distinguish irony from literal agreement.
premise: Coding application: 'Great, another delay' is irony under the stated contextual rule.
step: Inspect the supplied coding application; it resolves the alleged absence of an application.
result: Supplement defeats the material-absence concern, without proving the rule's universal validity.

text:
Group membership is the mechanism.
The manipulation changed both perceived membership and perceived norm violation.
premise: The manipulation changed both perceived membership and perceived norm violation.
step: A contrast compatible with both explanations does not identify membership alone.
result: The mechanism inference is underdetermined by these observations.

text:
Figure 1 proves a nonlinear trend.
Caption: Outcome by condition.
step: The caption supplies no inspectable evidence of the visual pattern.
result: Image evidence unavailable; do not invent figure contents.

text:
A larger trust score demonstrates greater cooperation.
The score contains attitude items only.
claim: A larger trust score demonstrates greater cooperation.
premise: The score contains attitude items only.
step: The construct interpretation needs a justified link from attitudes to cooperative behaviour.
result: Missing construct-to-behaviour premise; narrow the conclusion or supply relevant validity evidence.

text:
The scale is valid because it measures trust.
It measures trust because it is a valid trust scale.
claim: The scale is valid because it measures trust.
premise: It measures trust because it is a valid trust scale.
step: The premise restates the validity claim rather than providing independent support.
result: Circular support does not establish validity for this use.

text:
The coding distinguishes irony from literal agreement.
Identifiable interviews cannot be shared under consent; an anonymized coding explanation can be provided.
claim: The coding distinguishes irony from literal agreement.
premise: Identifiable interviews cannot be shared under consent; an anonymized coding explanation can be provided.
step: Assess the coding inference through a privacy-preserving explanation rather than demanding identifiable cases.
result: Unavailable cases do not establish missing author inspection; a bounded explanation may settle the inference.
